title: Claims Manual, Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan: Separate Settlement per Plan and the Rolling Claim Count
content:
## 1. Each plan is settled on its own

Each Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan is settled on its own. A loss that damages two rented units is two claims under two plans, each with its own limit, and each with its own deductible where the level provides that a loss affecting two units is settled as two claims with two deductibles.

## 2. Claim count in the rolling window

The plan pays at most the level's maximum number of claims with loss dates in the rolling window; a further claim is denied for the claim count limit (claim count limit reached).

The count is taken as follows:

- **Window.** The rolling 365 calendar days of loss dates ending on the loss date of the claim being decided, that day included, for the one plan.
- **What is counted.** The distinct claims of that plan that carry a claim payment not fully voided and whose loss date falls in the window.

### Points of judgement

| Situation in the plan's records | Counted? |
| --- | --- |
| A claim in the window paid and never voided | Yes |
| A claim in the window whose payment was partly voided | Yes (not fully voided) |
| A claim in the window whose payments were fully voided | No |
| A claim in the window with no claim payment | No |
| A paid claim whose loss date falls before the window | No |
| A paid claim under another plan of the same tenant | No (each plan is counted on its own) |

### Illustration (hypothetical)

On a level whose maximum is 2, a plan has two paid claims with loss dates 100 and 300 days before the loss date of a third claim. Both fall inside the 365-day window, so the plan has already paid 2 claims and the third claim is denied for the claim count limit. Had the earlier of the two loss dates been 400 days before, only 1 claim would be counted.

## 3. Former aggregate clause

The former clause under which the total paid on claims with loss dates in any rolling 365-day window could not exceed the coverage limit times the aggregate multiple of the level in force on the loss date being decided — an approval being reduced to the room left under that aggregate, and a claim with no room left being denied for the aggregate limit — is **no longer in force**. It has been superseded by the current basis for claim decisions.

superseded_clauses: Within one plan, the total paid on claims whose loss dates fall in any rolling 365-day window, measured by protect_msr_paid_365d, may not exceed coverage_limit_usd times aggregate_limit_multiple of the level in force on the loss date being decided; an approval is reduced to the room left under that aggregate, and a claim with no room left is denied with reason aggregate_limit_reached.
